_server: What power cord does the {name} need?
It depends on the PSU that is installed, not on the chassis. A PSU with a C14 inlet takes a C13 cord; a PSU with a C20 inlet takes a C19 cord. The table on this page lists which PSUs use which inlet.
Can I use a C13 cord on a C20 inlet?
No. C13 and C20 have different shapes and do not fit. A C20 inlet needs a C19 cord.
What cord goes from the {name} to a rack PDU?

Usually a short jumper with the same connector family at both ends: C13 to C14 for a C13 PDU outlet, or C19 to C20 for a C19 outlet. A wall plug cord (NEMA 5-15, Schuko, BS 1363) is only for a wall socket.
Should both PSUs go to the same PDU?
No. For redundancy plug each PSU into a different PDU on a different circuit (A and B feeds). Size each PDU so it can carry the whole server load alone.
_dgx: What power cord does the {name} need?

AC versions use 16/20 A class C19/C20 cords at 200–240 V. Check the exact cord set and count in the NVIDIA user guide listed on this page. Some models also ship in a DC busbar version that needs no AC cords.
Can a DGX run on 120 V?
Plan for 200–240 V. The power supplies are rated for high-line input, and 120 V circuits cannot deliver the load per cord that these systems need.
What PDU outlets does a DGX need?
C19 outlets, enough of them for every PSU, split across two PDUs on separate circuits for redundancy. C13 outlets cannot feed these PSUs.
How much power does a DGX rack need?
Several kilowatts per system. Use the maximum system power from the NVIDIA spec, add margin, and check it against the PDU and circuit with the PDU calculator.
c13-c14-server-power-cord: What is a C13 to C14 cord?
A jumper with a female C13 coupler on one end and a male C14 plug on the other. The C13 end goes into the server PSU, the C14 end into a C13 outlet on the PDU.
How many amps is a C13 to C14 cord?
10 A under IEC rules, and usually 15 A under UL rules in North America. Check the marking on the cord.
Is a C13 to C14 cord the same as a computer extension cable?
Yes. It is often sold as a monitor or PC extension cable. For racks, buy the length you need, usually 0.6 to 2 m.
c13-pdu-c19-server: Can I power a C20-inlet server from a C13 PDU outlet?
No. The C13 outlet is 10 A class and the C20 inlet is 16 A class. Adapters that do this are not safe for a full-load PSU.
Use a PDU with C19 outlets and a C19 to C20 jumper, or choose a lower-wattage PSU option for the server that has a C14 inlet.
Why do some PSUs have C20 inlets?
High-watt PSUs, usually about 2000 W and up, draw more current than a C13/C14 connection is rated for.
c13-to-c14-compatibility: Yes. C13 is the female coupler and C14 is the male inlet or plug. They are made to mate.
No. C16 has a notch that blocks C13. Use a C15 cord for a C16 inlet. A C15 cord also fits a C14 inlet.
No. C20 is a larger 16 A inlet and needs a C19 cord.
c13-to-c20-power-cord: What is a C13 to C20 cord for?
It feeds a server with a C14 inlet from a C19 outlet on a PDU. The C13 end goes into the server, the C20 end into the C19 outlet.
Is a C13 to C20 cord rated 16 A?
No. Its rating is set by the weaker C13 end, so treat it as a 10 A cord (15 A UL).
Can I use it the other way round?
No. A C20-inlet server needs a C19 cord. A C13 to C20 cord does not fit a C20 inlet.
c13-vs-c14: What is the difference between C13 and C14?
C13 is the female end (on the cord or a PDU outlet). C14 is the male end (the inlet on a server PSU, or the plug on a jumper).
Which one is on the server?
The server PSU has a C14 inlet. You plug a C13 cord into it.
Which one is on the PDU?
Most rack PDU outlets are C13. You plug the C14 end of a jumper into them.
c13-vs-c19: Yes. C19 is wider, with three flat pins in a row, and rated 16 A IEC (20 A UL). C13 is rated 10 A IEC (15 A UL).
Can I plug a C13 into a C19 outlet?
No. Use a C13 to C20 cord: C13 into the server, C20 into the C19 outlet.
How do I know if my server needs C13 or C19?
Look at the PSU inlet. A C14 inlet takes a C13 cord; a C20 inlet takes a C19 cord.
c19-c20-server-power-cord: What is a C19 to C20 cord?
A 16 A class jumper. The C19 end goes into a server PSU with a C20 inlet, the C20 end into a C19 outlet on the PDU.
What wire size do C19 to C20 cords use?
Usually 1.5 mm² (IEC) or 14 AWG / 12 AWG (UL) depending on the rating. Check the marking for 16 A or 20 A.
Do I need locking C19 cords?
Locking cords or outlets stop accidental unplugging in dense racks. They are optional unless your PDU or site requires them.
c19-to-c20-compatibility: Yes. C19 is the female coupler and C20 the male inlet or plug.
No. C19 is wider than a C14 inlet.
Yes. C21 is the high-temperature version and fits both C20 and C22 inlets. A C19 does not fit a C22.
c19-vs-c20: What is the difference between C19 and C20?
C19 is the female end (cord coupler or PDU outlet). C20 is the male end (PSU inlet or jumper plug).
What amp rating do C19 and C20 have?
16 A under IEC rules, usually 20 A under UL rules.
High-watt server PSUs, GPU servers, PDU inputs and UPS outputs.
dgx-h100-pdu-requirements: What PDU does a DGX H100 need?
PDUs with enough C19 outlets for all PSUs at 200–240 V, split across two feeds, with capacity for the full system power on each side.
How many power cords does a DGX H100 use?
The ship kit lists six C19/C20 class cords. Check the NVIDIA user guide for your exact configuration.
Can I use C13 outlets for a DGX H100?
No. The PSUs need C19 class connections.
how-many-servers-per-pdu: How many servers can one PDU power?
Divide the usable PDU power by the real server draw. Usable power is volts × amps (× 1.732 for three-phase), reduced to 80% for continuous load in North America.
Should I use nameplate watts or measured watts?
Measured or vendor-calculated typical draw gives a realistic count. Nameplate watts give a safe worst case. Use measured draw plus a margin of 20–30%.
Does A/B redundancy change the count?
Yes. With two PDUs each one must carry the whole load alone if the other feed fails, so size each PDU for the full rack.
pdu-power-cord-compatibility: How do I match a PDU and a server?
Compare the PDU outlet type (C13 or C19) with the server PSU inlet (C14 or C20) and pick the jumper that joins them.
What if the PDU has only C13 outlets and the server has C20 inlets?
There is no safe standard cord. Use a PDU with C19 outlets.
Yes. The PDU input (NEMA L6-30, IEC 60309 and others) must match the circuit and socket at the site.
power-connector-guide: Which numbers are male and which are female?
In IEC 60320 the odd number is the female end (coupler or outlet) and the even number is the male end (inlet or plug). C13 mates with C14, C19 with C20.
What is the most common rack connector?
C13/C14. Most PDU outlets are C13 and most 1U/2U server PSUs have C14 inlets.
What plug does a 208 V rack PDU use in the US?
Often NEMA L6-30 (30 A, 250 V, locking) for single-phase, or L21-30 for three-phase.
What plug does a 32 A PDU use in Europe or Africa?
Usually an IEC 60309 blue 2P+E 32 A plug for single-phase, or red 3P+N+E for three-phase.
server-to-pdu-power-cord: What cord connects a server to a PDU?
A jumper: C13 to C14 for C14-inlet servers on C13 outlets, C19 to C20 for C20-inlet servers on C19 outlets, or C13 to C20 for C14-inlet servers on C19 outlets.
What length should rack jumpers be?
As short as the route allows: often 0.6–1.2 m for 0U PDUs at the back of the same rack, 1.8–2 m when the PDU is further away.
Can I use the wall cord that came with the server?
Only if the PDU has matching wall-type sockets. Rack PDUs with C13/C19 outlets need IEC jumpers.
what-power-cord-does-my-server-need: How do I find out which power cord my server needs?
Read the inlet on the installed PSU (C14 or C20), then the outlet type on the PDU (C13 or C19), and pick the jumper that joins them.
Does the server model decide the cord?
No. The same chassis can ship with PSUs that have different inlets depending on wattage.
What if I plug the server into a wall socket?
Then you need a cord with the wall plug for your country on one end and C13 or C19 on the other.
pdu-calculator: How is usable PDU power calculated?
Volts × amps for single-phase, volts × amps × 1.732 for three-phase, then × 0.8 if you apply the North American continuous-load rule.
Why does the calculator ask for A/B feeds?
With redundant feeds each PDU must carry the whole load alone, so the server count is limited by one PDU.
Is the result enough to order hardware?
It is an estimate. Check breaker ratings, local code and the vendor power calculator for your exact configuration.
homelab-power-cost-calculator: How do I calculate the running cost of a server?
Watts × hours ÷ 1000 gives kWh. Multiply kWh by your price per kWh. A 100 W device running all month uses about 73 kWh.
Should I use idle or peak watts?
Use the average draw you measure with a power meter or the PDU. Peak watts overstate the bill.
What is the overhead percentage for?
It covers cooling, UPS losses and network gear that runs because of the servers.
